title: Clippers: Kawhi Leonard, Aspiration and the NBA's ruling
summary: The biggest off-court story of the offseason. The NBA concluded after a near-yearlong investigation that the Clippers helped arrange endorsement deals that paid Kawhi Leonard outside the salary cap, and handed down severe penalties.

items.x: Pablo Torre's podcast alleges the Clippers used sponsor Aspiration, backed by owner Steve Ballmer's money, to pay Leonard about $28 million for a no-show job. The Clippers deny it and the NBA opens an investigation.
Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg is sentenced to 14 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to two counts of wire fraud.
The Clippers agree in principle to trade Leonard to Toronto, with Brandon Ingram reported as the headline of the return. The deal is put on hold while the investigation is open.

The NBA rules: the Clippers forfeit five first-round picks (2029 through 2033), face a $30 million fine, and Leonard owes $700,000. Ballmer is suspended one year and team business president Gillian Zucker one year without pay. Basketball president Lawrence Frank is suspended six months without pay. Leonard's uncle, Dennis Robertson, is banned five years from doing business with NBA teams.

The league says its investigator found a pattern of misconduct, including off-court deals between Leonard and four companies tied to the team (Aspiration, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics and Lockton Insurance), and that the Clippers were a prior offender. The Clippers reject the findings and say they will challenge them, including through arbitration.
Toronto signs Leonard to a contract extension, per Basketball Reference's transaction log.
